newsitem.title: FRANCE: Castro, Arafat due in Paris for Mitterrand tribute.
newsitem.headline: Castro, Arafat due in Paris for Mitterrand tribute.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat are expected in Paris on Friday to pay tribute to late French president Francois Mitterrand, a year after his death, UNESCO said on Monday.

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, former U.N. secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali and former Israeli prime minister Shimon Peres were also expected to attend the second day of a January 9-10 symposium at UNESCO headquarters.

"Leading personalities from different parts of the world will offer personal tributes to the late president's contribution to peace and development," the U.N. Educational Scientific and Cultural Organisation said in a statement.
Paris-based UNESCO announced the symposium on December 10, entitled "Francois Mitterrand - Peace and Development - Tributes".
At that time, many of those invited had yet to reply. UNESCO said that all the leaders it listed had confirmed attendance but said Castro's acceptance was still provisional.

Socialist Mitterrand ruled France for 14 years until 1995 and was a tireless builder of European integration. He died on January 9, 1996 eight months after he was succeeded by conservative Jacques Chirac as president.
The symposium would be under Chirac's patronage.
Other speakers include former European Commission presidents Jacques Delors and Gaston Thorn, Senegalese Prime Minister Habib Thiam, Kazakhstan President Nursultan Nazarbayev.

Opinion polls show that most French people regard Mitterrand's record was positive, especially for social reforms such as cutting the working week, lowering the pension age to 60 from 65 and abolishing the death penalty.

But his image has been tarnished over the past year by allegations that he misled French people for more than a decade by hiding that he was suffering from cancer. He had come to power in 1981 promising openness about his health.
